name: Spain (since 1898)
summary: Spain after losing its last major colonies in 1898: a monarchy, a short republic, civil war (1936–39), Franco’s dictatorship (1939–75) and, since 1978, a parliamentary democracy.

knownFor.label: Guernica
knownFor.note: Picasso’s painting of the bombing of a Basque town.

knownFor.label: Sagrada Família
knownFor.note: Gaudí’s basilica in Barcelona, still being finished.

knownFor.label: Flamenco
knownFor.note: Song, dance and guitar music from Andalusia.

location.value: Most of the Iberian Peninsula, the Balearic and Canary Islands, and Ceuta and Melilla in North Africa.

terrain.value: A vast central plateau (the Meseta Central), the Pyrenees and other mountain ranges, and long coasts.

climate.value: Mostly Mediterranean, with hot, dry summers.

resources.value: Farmland (olives, wine, citrus), fish, tourism, sun and wind energy.
resources.source: Wikipedia: Spain; Wikipedia: Spanish Civil War

disasters.value: Droughts, wildfires and the Valencia floods (2024).
disasters.source: Wikipedia: Spain; Wikipedia: Spanish Civil War

population.value: 18.6 million in 1900; about two and a half times as many today, after a boom in the 1960s.

urbanisation.value: Madrid and Barcelona are the largest cities.

disease.value: The 1918 influenza (“Spanish flu”, named only because Spain’s press reported it freely).
disease.source: Wikipedia: Spain; Wikipedia: Spanish Civil War

migration.value: Emigration to Latin America and Europe; large immigration since the 1990s.
migration.source: Wikipedia: Spain; Wikipedia: Spanish Civil War

economicBase.value: Farming at first; from the 1960s industry and mass tourism; today services, tourism and exports.

tradeRoutes.value: Part of the EU single market since 1986.

wealth.source: Wikipedia: Spain; Wikipedia: Spanish Civil War

inequality.source: Wikipedia: Spain; Wikipedia: Spanish Civil War

governmentType.value: A parliamentary monarchy since the 1978 constitution.

keyRulers.value: Francisco Franco (1939–75); King Juan Carlos I; Adolfo Suárez; Felipe González; King Felipe VI.

succession.value: Elections to the Cortes; the king is head of state.
succession.source: Wikipedia: Spain; Wikipedia: Spanish Civil War

institutions.value: The 1978 constitution, the Cortes and autonomous communities.

stability.value: The Civil War (1936–39) and Franco’s dictatorship (1939–75); a failed coup on 23 February 1981; the armed Basque group ETA dissolved in 2018.

eliteConflict.value: Tensions over Catalan and Basque independence (Catalan referendum, 2017).

armyAndTech.source: Wikipedia: Spain; Wikipedia: Spanish Civil War

majorWars.value: The Rif War in Morocco (1921–26); the Spanish Civil War (1936–39).

territoryChange.value: Gave up its Moroccan protectorate (1956) and Equatorial Guinea (1968).
territoryChange.source: Wikipedia: Spain; Wikipedia: Spanish Civil War

alliancesRivals.value: Neutral in the First World War; joined NATO (1982) and the European Economic Community (1986).

inventions.value: High-speed rail network (AVE), one of the longest in the world.
inventions.source: Wikipedia: Spain; Wikipedia: Spanish Civil War

scienceEducation.value: Free public education; universities such as Salamanca (1218).
scienceEducation.source: Wikipedia: Spain; Wikipedia: Spanish Civil War

openness.value: Isolated under Franco, open since the 1970s.
openness.source: Wikipedia: Spain; Wikipedia: Spanish Civil War

communicationTransport.value: AVE high-speed trains (1992) and an extensive motorway network.
communicationTransport.source: Wikipedia: Spain; Wikipedia: Spanish Civil War

religion.value: Mostly Catholic by tradition; increasingly secular.
religion.source: Wikipedia: Spain; Wikipedia: Spanish Civil War

languageWriting.value: Spanish (Castilian); Catalan, Basque and Galician are co-official in their regions.

artsArchitecture.value: Painters Picasso, Dalí and Miró; Gaudí’s modernisme architecture; flamenco from Andalusia.

socialStructure.source: Wikipedia: Spain; Wikipedia: Spanish Civil War

sharedIdentity.value: Strong regional identities alongside a Spanish one.
sharedIdentity.source: Wikipedia: Spain; Wikipedia: Spanish Civil War

dailyLife.value: City apartments; tapas, paella, olive oil; late meals.
dailyLife.source: Wikipedia: Spain; Wikipedia: Spanish Civil War

neighbours.value: Portugal, France, Andorra, Morocco (across the strait).

ideasReligions.source: Wikipedia: Spain; Wikipedia: Spanish Civil War

colonisation.value: Lost Cuba, Puerto Rico and the Philippines in 1898.

peakPeriod.value: Growth after joining the EEC (1986) and adopting the euro (2002).

declineSignals.source: Wikipedia: Spain; Wikipedia: Spanish Civil War

outcome.source: Wikipedia: Spain; Wikipedia: Spanish Civil War

sources.source: Wikipedia: Spain; Wikipedia: Spanish Civil War
